data.title: HTX DAO Ambassador Molly: How to Become a Mature Investor
data.description:
On November 26, 2026, the 2026 Hong Kong Wealth Management Summit and the 13th "Hong Kong Stock Top 100" Awards Ceremony were held at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre. HTX DAO Ambassador Molly was invited to attend and participate in the roundtable discussion on "2027 Wealth Management and Asset Allocation." As a seasoned Web3 practitioner, Molly shared her thoughts on investment based on her long-term experience and observations in the industry. (This article is promotional content provided by HTX DAO and represents only its views, not the platform's position, and does not constitute investment advice.) With the continuous development of technology, traditional finance and Web3 are accelerating their integration, giving rise to a wider range of investment options. Molly pointed out that for investors, regardless of the market they enter, establishing a mature investment understanding is a must. She bluntly stated, "Without a mature and systematic investment strategy and mindset, choosing A-shares, gold, US stocks, or blockchain is just another avenue for losing money." Molly started by analyzing Bitcoin's price movements over the past few years. During Bitcoin's rise from $20,000 to $120,000, there were several significant pullbacks. Some investors who regretted missing out on the rise later found that the market gave them another chance to reassess. She stated that after experiencing several rounds of rises and falls, people's feelings about "missing out" change. If one believes that the current rise is the last opportunity, it's easy to bet too much capital at once out of fear of missing out. When the market changes and a more familiar and reliable opportunity arises, there's not much room left. Molly said, "What cycles teach us is not just risk management, but also believing that the market always offers opportunities. Always having some capital in hand ensures that you're still able to participate when the next opportunity arises." Knowing "buy low, sell high," why do people still chase highs and sell lows? The fluctuations in Bitcoin's price also showed Molly that the hardest thing to change in trading is often the investor's own behavioral habits. Originally intending to observe for a while longer, seeing the price steadily rise, they begin to worry that waiting will be too late. When the market suddenly reverses, even if the initial reasons for buying still hold true, they may hastily sell due to panic. "Buy low, sell high" is a principle almost everyone understands, but the real difficulty lies in being able to execute one's strategy and discipline when price fluctuations are most intense and emotions are amplified. In Molly's words, "Controlling emotions is itself part of investment ability." How is this ability developed? Molly uses the analogy of education. To get into a good university, people are willing to spend over a decade studying systematically, knowing that hard work doesn't guarantee success. But in the financial markets, people easily believe that a few pieces of information, some experience, and intuition are enough to consistently make money. Molly believes that investing is also a professional skill that requires long-term training. Analyzing assets and judging value can be gradually improved through learning and practice, while patience and execution need to be honed through repeated transactions. Furthermore, it requires continuous review and revision of past investment strategies. "Rather than searching for the next profitable market, we should think about how to become a mature investor." "Molly said."

Note: This article does not constitute investment advice, nor does it constitute an offer, solicitation of an offer, or recommendation for any investment product.

data.title: US Finds No Evidence of China-Directed Nvidia Spying, But Alice Huang's Troubles Continue
data.description:
US Intelligence Finds No Evidence Beijing Ordered Alice Huang to Spy on Nvidia

The espionage allegations surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang have taken another turn after US intelligence officials reportedly found no evidence that Beijing instructed Alice Huang to spy on the chipmaker's chief executive.

Attorney General Todd Blanche on Singapore banning Alice Huang from entering the country in February 2026: I don’t have any information… sometimes that certainly could result in action by the United States and sometimes it doesn’t result in any action. https://t.co/ICYhjbbdY9

— NewsNewsNews (@RealCrookedNews) November 12, 2026

Officials delivered the assessment to congressional staffers on Tuesday, according to The Wall Street Journal, which cited people familiar with the classified briefing. Although Alice Huang reportedly contacted China's intelligence service during the affair, officials found no indication that she had passed on significant intelligence.

The assessment could still change if new evidence emerges, but the findings represent a significant development in a controversy that has drawn attention to Silicon Valley, US national security and China's access to advanced American technology.

Spy or not, did Alice Huang-controlled Megaspeed actually smuggle $1B+ worth of Nvidia chips into China? The evidence tells conflicting stories. Review and trade the evidence on Verifact: https://t.co/COHJBJRHGP https://t.co/u2Gclt9mOe

— Verifact Markets (@verifact) November 13, 2026

Despite the latest intelligence findings, Alice Huang's situation remains unresolved. The former Megaspeed International executive continues to face entry restrictions in Singapore and Taiwan, while US authorities have added her former company and several related businesses to their trade blacklist.

How Alice Huang Became Entangled in Nvidia's National Security Controversy

Also known by her Chinese name, Huang Le, Alice Huang is a Hong Kong resident who previously led Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud computing company that became a major Nvidia customer.

Megaspeed originally operated as the overseas subsidiary of a Chinese video game business before shifting its focus toward artificial intelligence infrastructure. The company subsequently became an official Nvidia cloud partner in November 2023.

The US has added Singapore-based Megaspeed to its trade blacklist over allegations of sending Nvidia chips to China, cutting the firm off from American technology amid a Justice Department criminal probe. https://t.co/6D4jvCKyb2

— TaiwanPlus News (@taiwanplusnews) November 24, 2026

However, Huang's formal position within the company has been the subject of differing corporate and regulatory records. According to records cited by the Associated Press, she ceased to be a registered director of Megaspeed in November 2023.

Singaporean authorities nevertheless identified her as the company's chief executive, chairperson and a key controller when they investigated its activities in 2025.

Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said the country will keep investigating Megaspeed, an Nvidia-linked cloud firm accused by US authorities of diverting advanced AI chips to China. The US added the Singapore-based firm to its trade blacklist https://t.co/B6T8jA1H9W https://t.co/be531RwyYd

— Reuters (@Reuters) November 24, 2026

Megaspeed later said on November 15 that Huang had formally departed on August 30, 2025, and no longer held any position within the company. The firm declined to comment on her private affairs while maintaining that its business operations were lawful.

Singapore and Taiwan Bar Alice Huang Despite Lack of Espionage Evidence

Alice Huang's problems with Singaporean authorities began before the espionage allegations became public.

Singapore launched an investigation in February 2025 into suspected false declarations involving purchases of computer servers and their eventual destinations. Police questioned Huang in June that year and retained her passport to ensure she remained available during the investigation.

Just in: US stock markets leapt higher on Monday, as the AI trade reignited following the return of Jensen Huang as Nvidia chief executive. https://t.co/C2sQ61Eur8 https://t.co/rmJZWqtD9C

— Financial Times (@FT) November 23, 2026

In February 2026, authorities determined that there was insufficient evidence to establish that she had committed offences related to the suspected false declarations.

However, Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs said investigators believed Huang had knowingly provided inaccurate information to minimize her involvement in Megaspeed.

🚨🇺🇸 US Intelligence Flags Possible Chinese Surveillance of Alice Huang! CBS News Reports Fresh National Security Concerns US intelligence officials have reportedly raised concerns that China's Ministry of State Security (MSS) may have monitored Alice Huang, following her reported relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. According to CBS News, intelligence officials briefed congressional staffers about the matter, highlighting potential counterintelligence risks involving China's intelligence network and the US semiconductor industry. 📌 Key Developments: 🔹 Spring 2025: US intelligence agencies reportedly identified Alice Huang's contact with an MSS officer. 🔹 Congressional Briefing: Intelligence officials from multiple US agencies briefed House and Senate Intelligence Committee staffers. 🔹 Classified Memorandum: Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly prepared a memorandum outlining intelligence concerns. 🔹 Megaspeed Connection: Alice Huang previously held a senior position at Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is under US investigation over alleged diversion of sensitive American technology to China. 🔹 Jensen Huang: Nvidia's CEO is expected to face congressional scrutiny over related national security concerns. ⚠️ What US Intelligence Has Not Established: No evidence so far that Alice Huang was directed to gather information specifically about Jensen Huang. No evidence so far that she shared information of substantial intelligence value with China. China has rejected the allegations that Alice Huang is a spy. 🏭 Why This Matters for the Tech Industry: The case raises broader questions about: 1️⃣ Semiconductor export controls. 2️⃣ Protection of advanced AI technology. 3️⃣ Corporate due diligence and national security. 4️⃣ Cross-border technology supply chains. 5️⃣ Intelligence risks involving strategic technology companies. 💡 The Bigger Picture: The controversy highlights the growing intersection of artificial intelligence, international business and geopolitical security. Nvidia's global operations and the movement of advanced AI chips are attracting increasing scrutiny from US policymakers. 📲 Follow Varta24 Business for the latest AI, semiconductor, technology and global business developments. #Nvidia #JensenHuang #AliceHuang #China #USIntelligence #NationalSecurity #ArtificialIntelligence #Semiconductors #ChipIndustry #Geopolitics #TechnologyNews #Varta24Business

— Varta24 Business (@Varta24Business) November 26, 2026

She subsequently received a formal warning and was prohibited from returning to Singapore. Authorities returned her passport on February 26, and she left the country that same day. Taiwanese authorities have also revoked her entry permit, adding another restriction to her international movements.

Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong reiterated the government's position while speaking in Australia on Tuesday, saying there were no grounds to prosecute Huang, although investigations into Megaspeed were continuing.

Singapore has also explicitly clarified that its investigation into Huang was unrelated to espionage.

Alice Huang's Whereabouts and Business Connections Remain Under Scrutiny

While the intelligence findings have weakened the allegations of a Beijing-directed espionage operation, questions surrounding Alice Huang's whereabouts and business connections remain unanswered.

Bloomberg reported on November 12, citing anonymous sources, that Huang was in Beijing and that Chinese security officials were aware of her presence there. However, her current whereabouts have not been independently confirmed.

Alice Huang, the woman at the center of the scandal engulfing Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, has returned to China and is in Beijing, according to Bloomberg’s exclusive reporting. The chipmaker is investigating spying allegations denied by Beijing. @allenwan290 reports: https://t.co/FD2orrtHX6

— Bloomberg (@business) November 12, 2026

Beijing has rejected the espionage allegations, while Huang herself has remained publicly silent in recent reporting.

Meanwhile, scrutiny of her wider business network has intensified. Reuters reported on Wednesday that companies connected to Huang's relatives and business associates had secured financing against artificial intelligence servers and computing modules valued at approximately $270 million in China.

However, the financial records did not establish whether the equipment contained chips subject to US export restrictions. Huang could not be reached for comment by Reuters.

US Blacklists Megaspeed as Questions Surround Its AI Hardware Connections

The latest developments come after Washington added Megaspeed and several related businesses to its trade blacklist on Monday, further intensifying scrutiny of the company's connections to China's artificial intelligence industry.

The Trump administration added Megaspeed International and six affiliates to the Commerce Department's Entity List on Monday, citing a risk that the Singapore-based cloud computing company could divert advanced artificial intelligence chips to unauthorized users. https://t.co/peiATx3aeb

— The Washington Times (@WashTimes) November 24, 2026

The decision adds another dimension to the controversy, particularly as US authorities seek to restrict China's access to advanced American AI technology.

Although the latest intelligence assessment found no evidence that Beijing instructed Alice Huang to spy on Jensen Huang, it does not resolve the separate questions surrounding Megaspeed's commercial activities and its business connections.

Singapore said it disagrees with the US findings that the city-state’s policies contribute to excess manufacturing capacity and will urge Washington to reconsider proposed tariffs of up to 20% on its exports. https://t.co/nPWEec9gDI

— Bloomberg (@business) November 26, 2026

For now, Jensen Huang has returned to the helm of Nvidia following his brief departure, while Alice Huang remains largely out of public view.

The espionage allegations may have lost some ground, but the wider controversy surrounding Megaspeed, its business network and the movement of advanced AI hardware between China and international markets remains unresolved.

data.title: Ethereum Foundation's coin sale: No impact on Ethereum's fundamentals
data.description:
1. Is there a relationship between the project and the token value?

Whether there is a relationship between the project and the token depends on the situation:

If the project value has a suitable channel to be reflected in the token, then in the long run, there will definitely be a relationship between the project and the token value;

Otherwise, there may be no relationship between the project and the token value at all.

What does "the project value has a suitable channel to be reflected in the token" mean?

First, it depends on whether the project itself generates cash flow;

Second, it depends on whether the project team can return the generated cash flow to token holders.

In the crypto ecosystem, token buybacks are a very common way of giving back. This is even more evident in the traditional stock market:

Generally, what we call "good companies" in the traditional stock market have this behavior, either buying back and burning shares or paying cash dividends to shareholders. There is another type of company that neither pays dividends nor buys back shares; in that case, we need to see if the company uses its cash flow to strengthen its competitive advantage.

If a project/company neither pays dividends, nor repurchases tokens, nor uses its money wisely for business but instead squanders it, then in this case, the project/company has nothing to do with its stock/token value. I used to often cite Uniswap as an example, saying that the project was good, but its token value was questionable, precisely because at that time its cash flow had no channel to feed back into its token, so there was no relationship between its project and token value. Of course, it has improved now, with buybacks, which is a good improvement. 2. The Ethereum Foundation has been selling Ethereum, why do you think it still has potential? In the current fundamentals, not to mention the Ethereum Foundation selling tokens, even if BMNR sells tokens, it won't affect my view on Ethereum. I've written too many articles about the reasons. This question reminds me of another type of article I wrote before, which is about founders or core teams selling stocks/tokens. I've previously cited two examples: one is the sale of shares by a special figure within Tencent more than a decade ago, and the other is the sale of shares by Nvidia's Huang (Jensen Huang). In the Tencent case, someone with extremely close ties to the founder sold shares shortly after the company's IPO and during subsequent events. In the Nvidia case, Huang repeatedly sold shares, similarly sparking considerable external scrutiny and speculation. These actions each triggered public panic, especially the Tencent sales, which repeatedly drew strong media scrutiny and suspicions of potential illegal profiteering using insider information. However, on the other hand, many investors were optimistic about Tencent and Nvidia, buying and holding their shares at this time. Looking back over the years, these investors who weathered the storms have achieved far greater returns than those who sold their shares initially. In these two cases, Tencent's case has been repeatedly cited by well-known investors to illustrate this point: often, even the founders of a company may not have a deep enough understanding of it, and may not be able to recognize its potential and value. My purpose in citing these cases in the article was not to suggest that we should be indifferent to these events, but rather to say that investment is not necessarily based on someone's high status or special identity, which guarantees their actions are "smart" or their views are "accurate." No matter how big the external "turmoil" or how great the external "influence," its true impact on the intrinsic value of a company often has nothing to do with their status or identity. Ultimately, investment must return to the three criteria I've shared: corporate culture, business model/moat, and a suitable price. In other words, did these "events" actually affect the corporate culture, business model/moat, and suitable price? If we don't return to these three criteria and don't think these questions through, then naturally we'll become nervous and suspicious at the slightest external disturbance. Returning to Ethereum, my examples of Tencent and Nvidia are not to say that the Ethereum Foundation doesn't understand Ethereum's potential and value, nor am I trying to judge whether its actions are right or wrong. Rather, I want to say that, based on the three criteria mentioned above, these actions by the Ethereum Foundation do not affect my assessment of Ethereum at all. The Ethereum Foundation selling tokens is not the most unusual thing; there's also Vitalik selling tokens, BMNR selling tokens, traditional US financial capital selling tokens, and so on. If you buy/hold Ethereum without carefully considering these issues, there will be countless problems to worry about in the future, leading to endless anxieties and concerns.

data.title: A retrospective analysis of QQQ's ten major drawdowns over its 27-year history: Will the AI ​​boom repeat itself this time?
data.description:
Author: Biteye Source: X, @BiteyeCN

Similarly, with the tech stock crash, some people broke even in three months after buying at the bottom, while others waited 16 years.

...

In 2000, when the dot-com bubble burst, QQQ plummeted by 83%; during the 2008 global financial crisis, QQQ was halved; during the 2020 pandemic, QQQ dropped nearly 30% in less than a month.

Now, with increasing concerns about an AI bubble, QQQ has once again experienced a pullback of nearly 20%.

TL;DR

  • Monetary Tightening: Fed rate hikes and balance sheet reduction are common triggers for tech stock crashes.
  • Frequency of Drawdowns: Since 2020, QQQ has seen more frequent drawdowns exceeding 20%.
  • Recovery Cycle: Declines triggered by external shocks usually recover quickly, while the bursting of valuation bubbles can lead to a prolonged bear market.
  • Narrative Risk: From the internet to AI, when corporate profits fail to meet market expectations, popular narratives can also become the trigger for a crash.
  • Narrative Risk:

    • TL;DR

    • Monetary Tightening: Fed rate hikes and balance sheet reduction are common triggers for tech stock crashes.
    • Drawdown Frequency: Since 2020, QQQ has seen more frequent drawdowns exceeding 20%.
    • Recovery Cycle: Declines triggered by external shocks usually recover quickly, while the bursting of valuation bubbles can lead to a prolonged bear market.
    • Narrative Risk:

      • TL;DR

      • Narrative Risk: From the internet to AI, when corporate profits fail to meet market expectations, popular narratives can also become the trigger for a crash.
      • Narrative Risk:

      2000: The Dot-com Bubble Burst

      • Drawdown Period: March 27, 2000 – October 9, 2002
      • Maximum Drawdown: 83.0%

      In the late 1990s, personal computers and the internet rapidly became widespread, and portal websites and e-commerce became the hottest investment narratives in the capital market. Companies such as Yahoo, Amazon, and Cisco were highly sought after.

      2004: Recovery After the Dot-com Bubble and the First Interest Rate Hike

      • Drawdown Time: January 26, 2004 – August 12, 2004
      • Maximum Drawdown: Approximately 15.9%

      After the dot-com bubble burst, the Federal Reserve lowered interest rates to 1%, and the US economy gradually recovered. Broadband internet, search engines, and personal computers became the growth hotspots in the technology industry, and Google also went public that year."> However, economic recovery and rising international oil prices exacerbated inflation concerns, and the Federal Reserve began a new round of interest rate hikes in June 2004. The market began to digest the valuation pressure brought by monetary tightening in advance. 2006: Globalization Boom and Inflation Crisis Drawdown Time: January 11, 2006 – July 21, 2006 Maximum Drawdown: 17.4% At that time, the global market was dominated by investment narratives about the BRIC countries and the commodity supercycle. The rapid development of emerging economies like China and the booming US real estate market led investors to widely anticipate a soft landing for the economy. At the time, the global market was dominated by investment narratives focusing on the BRIC countries and the commodity supercycle. However, international oil prices approached $80, and the Federal Reserve raised interest rates 17 times consecutively, from 1% to 5.25%. Market concerns arose that continued monetary tightening would lead to an economic recession, resulting in a sell-off of technology stocks. 2007: The Housing Bubble and the Global Financial Crisis Drawdown Period: October 31, 2007 – November 20, 2008 Maximum Drawdown: Approximately 53.4% ​​At that time, the US housing market had experienced years of prosperity, and Wall Street was rife with financial innovation, using financial products such as MBS and CDOs to package and sell housing loans, believing that this method could diversify risk. However, as house prices fell and mortgage default rates rose, these financial products rapidly depreciated. In 2008, Lehman Brothers went bankrupt, triggering a global liquidity crisis. To repay debts and cope with redemptions, financial institutions were forced to sell off large amounts of assets, and technology stocks were not spared. 2011: The Rise of Mobile Internet and the Sovereign Debt Crisis Drawdown Period: July 26, 2011 – August 19, 2011 Maximum Drawdown: Approximately 16.1% After the financial crisis, the Federal Reserve stimulated the economy through quantitative easing. Meanwhile, iPhone, Android, mobile internet, and social networks became the new narrative in the technology industry. However, the European sovereign debt crisis continued to escalate, with countries like Greece facing debt repayment difficulties. The United States also experienced its first sovereign credit rating downgrade by Standard & Poor's in August due to the debt ceiling controversy. The United States also suffered its first sovereign credit rating downgrade by Standard & Poor's in August due to the debt ceiling dispute. Global markets began to worry about government debt risks and a double-dip recession, causing tech stocks to fall. 2018: The FAANG Bull Market Encountered Interest Rate Hikes and Trade War

      Drawdown Time: August 29, 2018 – December 24, 2018

      Maximum Drawdown: 23.2%

      However, the Federal Reserve raised interest rates four times throughout 2018 while simultaneously reducing its balance sheet. Coupled with the escalation of the US-China trade war, the market began to lower its expectations for the global economy and the profits of technology companies, causing QQQ to fall into a technical bear market.

      2020: The COVID-19 Pandemic and the Global Economic Shutdown

      • Drawdown Time: February 19, 2020 – March 16, 2020
      • Maximum Drawdown: 28.6%

      At the beginning of 2020, 5G, cloud computing, and electric vehicles became popular investment areas in the technology industry. The signing of the first phase of the trade agreement between China and the United States raised market expectations for a global economic recovery. However, the COVID-19 pandemic suddenly swept the globe, causing factory shutdowns, flight cancellations, and a standstill in consumer activity. The US stock market triggered circuit breakers four times in just ten days. Subsequently, the Federal Reserve launched large-scale quantitative easing, and the pandemic also spurred new demands such as remote working and e-commerce, leading to a rapid rebound in technology stocks.

      2021: The End of the Zero Interest Rate Frenzy

      • Drawdown Time: 2021.11.19—2022.12.28
      • Maximum Drawdown: 35.6%

      Driven by zero interest rates and large-scale quantitative easing, investment narratives such as electric vehicles, metaverse, SPACs, meme stocks, and NFTs have successively exploded, and global risk assets have ushered in a frenzy."> However, the Federal Reserve's previous assessment that inflation was only temporary has gradually become ineffective. Coupled with the Russia-Ukraine conflict, the US CPI rose 9.1% year-on-year in June 2022.

      2025: The AI ​​Bull Market Encounters the Impact of Trump's Tariffs

      • Drawdown Time: 2025.02.19—2025.04.08
      • Maximum Drawdown: 22.9%

      After ChatGPT ignited the AI ​​revolution, GPUs, large-scale models, and AI data centers became global investment hotspots, and the "Magnificent Seven" of US stocks became the main driving force of the bull market. ">After ChatGPT ignited the AI ​​revolution, GPUs, large-scale models, and AI data centers became global investment hotspots, and the "Magnificent Seven" of US stocks became the main driving force of the bull market. "> Meanwhile, the market was also trading in the benefits of Trump's tax cuts and deregulation policies. However, on April 2nd, Trump announced large-scale retaliatory tariffs, causing market concerns about rising global supply chain costs, inflation, and economic recession, leading to a concentrated sell-off in tech stocks. Will 2026 be a major valuation test for the AI ​​industry?

      • Drawdown Period: October 6, 2026 – November 20, 2026
      • Maximum Drawdown During the Period: 19.9%

      AI investment narrative is gradually expanding from large models and GPUs to AI Agents, computing power leasing, data centers, electricity, and AI infrastructure financing.

      As tech giants continue to expand their capital expenditures, the market is beginning to question whether AI commercial revenue can cover the huge investment costs and whether the debt accumulated from data center construction is sustainable. Entering November, management changes at Nvidia, reports of an SEC investigation into its accounting practices, coupled with higher-than-expected US inflation and rising expectations of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike, further dampened market confidence. Are tech stock plunges becoming more frequent?

      Reviewing QQQ's historical price movement, Biteye discovered an interesting phenomenon:

      From 2010 to 2019, QQQ only experienced a drawdown of more than 20% in one year, while it has occurred three times in the last seven years. The current AI market correction also approached 20% at one point.

data.title: Liu Jiaolian: Cryptocurrency hoarding company sells coins to pay off debts
data.description:
Overnight, Bitcoin (BTC) continued to recover upwards, and by this morning it had risen back above 61k. The dark clouds on the horizon have not yet dissipated, and asset management firm 21Shares even gave an extreme scenario of $43,800 (see today's internal report "The 60,000 Mark: Sufficient Surrender, Not Yet Confirmed").

Today's internal report also mentioned another observation: as the bear market drags on, people's patience is slowly being worn down, and now even the patience of companies—those treasury companies that hoard coins—is about to run out.

On November 25, the mNAV on the dashboard of Strategy, the largest coin hoarding company, once reported 0.88, and then rose to 0.94. On the same day, the ratio of enterprise value to coin value calculated by the analyst team led by Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou of JPMorgan Chase was also 0.88, lower than 0.89 in late June this year, setting a new low [1].

What does this number mean?

0.88 means that for every dollar of value a company holds in cryptocurrency, the market is only willing to pay $0.88. This indicator is called mNAV. The algorithm is not complicated. It is calculated by dividing the common stock price by the net BTC holding value per share, while taking into account debt, preferred stock equity and dollar assets [1]. In a bull market, it can be 1.5 or 2.0, and the market is willing to pay a premium for holding cryptocurrency; in a bear market, it falls below 1, and the premium becomes a discount.

It is not surprising that a discount occurs, but a long-term discount in a bear market will cause a cryptocurrency holding company to experience the torment of going from heaven to hell.

What cryptocurrency holding companies are betting on is, to put it bluntly, a value-added flywheel: when the stock price is higher than the value of holding cryptocurrency, they issue more shares to exchange for money, use the money to buy cryptocurrency, the number of coins per share increases, the stock price rises again, and they issue more shares. When this cycle is running, the company does not need to sell products or earn cash flow. As long as the price of cryptocurrency does not collapse, the financing will not stop. In the past two years, this model has been copied by many companies. The few companies that copied it the most have seen their stock prices rise more than BTC. During a bull market, the stocks of cryptocurrency hoarding companies appear to be leveraged Bitcoin. This means that buying their stock is equivalent to indirectly hoarding cryptocurrency with leverage. It sounds too good to be true, but what's the cost? Clearly, the cost is that the flywheel stops or even reverses during a bear market. The profits gained in the bull market are wiped out, principal and interest, in the bear market. Leveraging funds to hoard Bitcoin is a clever scheme devised by savvy investors. The more glorious the bull-bear cycle, the more devastating the crash – this is the grand calculation of fate. In a bear market, the price drops, the flywheel stops spinning, and the financing channels are tightened. Once the channels are shut down, the financial situation of cryptocurrency hoarding companies immediately worsens. If they can't survive the bear market, they have no choice but to sell cryptocurrency to pay off debts. Rest assured, fate has already calculated this; the bear market will allow enough leverage to pay off the debts. The bear market won't end until enough leverage is wiped out. Otherwise, it would be unfair to those who don't use leverage. The rise of this round of coin-hoarding companies using off-exchange leverage and on-exchange coin hoarding might be one of the reasons for the prolonged bear market. Why? ChainThink believes that in previous bear markets, leverage was concentrated within the cryptocurrency market, making liquidations smooth and efficient, allowing for rapid clearing within about a year before the market bottomed out and recovered. However, in this round, the leverage of coin-hoarding companies is in the stock market. A drop in the crypto market alone cannot directly trigger leverage; it can only suppress prices, wear down their patience, and force them to liquidate themselves. This results in low liquidation efficiency and slow clearing, causing prices to drop to around $60,000 very early in this cycle (the first dip in February 2026), but the bottoming process has been exceptionally long. While previous bottoms typically occurred within 12 to 13.5 months, this round has already dragged on for 13.7 months, and the reversal is still not complete. Many people are eagerly anticipating the Strategy liquidation in this bear market. However, its current pressure is mainly focused on the STRC preferred stock, and its overall financial situation is still relatively robust. However, other imitators are not so stable and lucky. Today's internal report mentioned that Kairos Research's on-chain statistics show that in the past few weeks, five companies, Silvia, Bit Digital, BTCS, Upexi and Solana Company, sold a total of about 410 BTC, 57,300 ETH and 986,000 SOL, which amounted to about $203 million based on the price on the day of the transfer [2]. The reasons for their selling can almost all be found on their balance sheets. BTCS sold when ETH fell to $1,561 to repay Aave's loan; Upexi sold when SOL was close to the loan collateral ratio warning line to bring the collateral ratio back to a safe level; Bit Digital sold to repay loans after the value of ETH collateral decreased [2]. None of the three companies said that they had changed their long-term views on BTC or ETH, they were just cornered by debt. Silvia, Solana Company, and Upexi listed many significant post-quarter events in their Q3 10-Q filings in November, but notably omitted any mention of the crypto asset sales that had already occurred, suggesting a possible lag of several months [2]. Since mid-October, approximately 25 treasury and mining companies have disclosed crypto asset sales in their SEC filings, with MARA disclosing approximately 13,600 BTC and Riot approximately 20,300 BTC [2]. Kairos Research cautions that Nakamoto, Upexi, and Solana Company still face loan liquidation pressures and may be among the next companies forced to sell [2]. This bear market is a slow, gradual process. When the knife has reached the seemingly rock-solid companies holding cryptocurrencies, and the combined pressure of time and price forces them to liquidate, the market is one step closer to spring. But before that, the pressure from their liquidation will inevitably bring painful pain to the market.

data.title: Australia's ClearAds Launches Trust Mark Badge To Help Consumers Spot Genuine Ads Amid Rising AI Scams
data.description:
ClearAds Introduces Trust Mark Badge To Help Australians Identify Independently Reviewed Advertisements

As AI-generated advertisements and online scams become harder to distinguish from genuine promotions, ClearAds is giving legitimate advertisers a way to show consumers that their campaigns have undergone independent checks.

Its new Trust Mark badge allows approved advertisements to display a verification label, helping audiences identify marketing content that has been reviewed against Australian advertising requirements.

Trust Mark Targets Growing Concerns Over Fake Ads And Misleading Promotions

The launch addresses growing concerns about advertising credibility, particularly across digital and social media platforms where fake endorsements and misleading promotions can reach large audiences.

According to the National Anti-Scam Centre, Australians reportedly lost AUD $2.18 billion to scams in 2025.

Smartraveller has issued a warning to Australians ahead of the holiday season. In 2025 alone, Australians reported losing more than $2.18 billion to scams, with travel-related scams a common tactic used by criminals. https://t.co/S3WDfjnoCspic.twitter.com/uN4h5XY2u5

— SBS News (@SBSNews) November 21, 2026

Meanwhile, Kantar's 2024 Media Reactions study found that Australian consumers were more sceptical of advertising than the global average.

AI has added another challenge by making it easier to produce convincing fake advertisements and endorsements.

This has also created difficulties for legitimate businesses, which must invest time and resources to ensure their campaigns meet advertising standards while competing for consumer attention.

ClearAds Director Alison Lee said,

"Over the past decade we have seen a sharp rise in scam and misleading advertising, especially in less regulated channels like social and digital media.

AI has accelerated these challenges, making it easier than ever to create convincing fake ads and misleading endorsements, and it is increasingly difficult for consumers to know what's real and what isn't.

That's a real business challenge for responsible advertisers who are investing significant time, money and effort into ensuring their advertising meets the relevant standards. Much of that work happens behind the scenes, so consumers have little visibility or understanding of the checks that have taken place."

Trust Mark aims to make those checks more visible by allowing consumers to recognise advertisements that have received independent approval.

Lee said,

"Trust Mark puts independent advertising approval front and centre, giving legitimate brands a way to demonstrate their commitment to responsible advertising and helping consumers identify advertising that has undergone an independent check.”

How Does The Trust Mark Badge Work Across Advertising Platforms?

The free, optional badge is available to eligible advertisers and agencies whose advertisements have been reviewed by ClearAds.

It can be used across television, radio, digital, social media, cinema and out-of-home advertising formats.

Importantly, Trust Mark applies only to the individual advertisement assessed and approved by ClearAds.

It is not a general endorsement of the advertiser, its products or all its marketing activities.

The initiative is intended to give consumers greater visibility into the checks behind advertising campaigns, particularly as businesses increasingly distribute the same promotions across different platforms.

Lee said,

"As brands increasingly run campaigns across multiple platforms, we think there's a real opportunity to make that accountability more visible, particularly in digital and social environments where consumers are understandably questioning what they see."

ClearAds, part of Free TV Australia, has provided independent advertising review and classification services since 1998.

Its work helps advertisers and agencies meet relevant requirements and reduce the risk of campaign delays, edits and reshoots.

Brand Developers Tests Trust Mark In Television Campaigns

Brand Developers, a direct-to-consumer marketing company operating in Australia and New Zealand, participated in the Trust Mark pilot programme.

The company tested the badge in television campaigns for two consumer products.

One product sold out during its initial launch, and Brand Developers has continued using Trust Mark in its advertising.

A company spokesperson said transparent advertising was important in helping customers make informed purchasing decisions.

"Participating in the ClearAds Trust Mark pilot programme has given us the opportunity to explore an additional way of communicating the advertising review process to consumers.

It's been a positive experience participating in the pilot programme and having the opportunity to provide feedback as ClearAds continues to develop the initiative.

The Trust Mark offers advertisers an additional way to communicate the importance they place on clear and transparent advertising."

Can An Advertising Verification Badge Restore Consumer Trust In The Age Of AI Scams?

Coinlive believes Trust Mark addresses a genuine problem, but its effectiveness will depend on whether consumers recognise and understand what the badge actually verifies.

Independent approval of an advertisement is useful, yet it does not automatically guarantee that a company, product or every future campaign is trustworthy.

The bigger challenge for ClearAds is turning a compliance label into something consumers actively look for, rather than another badge that gets overlooked among the growing number of online trust claims.

data.title: Monad, the last public blockchain to launch $183 million worth of tokens, faces a major test.
data.description:
Author: Michael Mach Source: X, @1912212eth

16.61 billion MON have ended their lock-up period, and the circulating supply has increased by 1.8 times.

As of press time, MON has rebounded to around $0.011, but the current price is still halved from the public sale price of $0.025 (a drop of 55.7%), and has cumulatively retreated more than 77% from the historical high of $0.04876 a year ago.

On the one-year anniversary unlocking date, the team released 10.7% (approximately 10.7 billion) of the initial total supply according to the rules, while investors and Category Labs' vault, having survived the one-year cliff period, released 25% (approximately 5.91 billion) of their holdings, resulting in a total unlocked amount of 16.61 billion tokens in a single day. As a result, the circulating supply of MON surged from approximately 9.2 billion before the unlock to 25.81 billion tokens, an increase of approximately 1.8 times in a single day.">On the one-year anniversary unlocking date, the team released 10.7% (approximately 10.7 billion) of the initial total supply according to the rules, while investors and Category Labs' vault, having survived the cliff period, released 25% (approximately 5.91 billion) of their holdings, resulting in a total unlocked amount of 16.61 billion tokens in a single day.

Locking up tokens to earn interest, 368 million tokens are being withdrawn from staking

Beyond short-term speculation, the on-chain ledger exposes more hidden cracks in the distribution of profits.

According to data from the MonadVision browser, the total staked amount on the network is currently approximately 22.3 billion MON, with the staking ratio remaining around 22% of the current total supply. The annualized staking yield (APR) is approximately 7.4%, maintained by active validator nodes such as Backpack, Kraken, Figment, and Alchemy. This means that over the past year, the vast majority of staking rewards have actually been pocketed by the Monad Foundation (through the validator delegation program VDP). The foundation has been steadily earning over 7% inflation on-chain using nominally 'ecosystem development' tokens. The 16.61 billion team and institutional tokens that were just unlocked on the first anniversary are now officially eligible to participate in staking and share the rewards. CoinMarketCap data further confirms this dilution effect: MON's current total supply has inflated from the initial 100 billion to 101.86 billion, with a maximum supply of 114.16 billion, and a net increase of approximately 1.86 billion (about $20.46 million) in the year since its launch; In contrast, the mainnet's cumulative burn volume is only about 87.94 million tokens, which is less than 5% of the annual inflation rate. Early large holders relied on locking up their tokens to earn interest and continuously lower their costs, while those buying in the secondary market had to bear the bitter consequences of inflation alone.

Buying but Not Burning: Why Doesn't the Project Team Burn the MON?

Amid persistent inflationary concerns, the market once expected the project team to launch a "buyback and burn" program, but Monad's "burning" and "buyback" are completely separate. The approximately 87.94 million MON already burned on-chain are all due to the automatic burning of the gas base fee compatible with EIP-1559, and are unrelated to the project team's financial operations.

The approximately 87.94 million MON already burned on-chain are all due to the automatic burning of the gas base fee compatible with EIP-1559, and are unrelated to the project team's financial operations.

As long as on-chain transaction activity does not improve, protocol-level destruction will be difficult to scale up. On the capital side, although the Monad system launched two support plans this year, both adopted a "buy-only, don't burn" strategy: the core development team, Category Labs, expanded its public market purchase authorization limit to $80 million (valid until the end of this year), but the purchased tokens were directly included in the company's reserves and not put into the black hole address; The Monad Foundation also allocated up to $60 million in August to launch a "limited liquidity program" for early investors, allowing institutions to sell back locked tokens at a discount. However, the buyback amount still follows the original lock-up period, and the nominal total supply and fully diluted valuation (FDV) are not reduced as a result. However, the early investor buyback program ultimately saw "limited actual participation." For low-cost seed round institutions, even with the current price falling by more than half from the public price of $0.025, they still have considerable unrealized profits, naturally lacking the incentive to exit at a discount. Meanwhile, although the foundation has stated that it will not sell tokens directly through over-the-counter (OTC) trading, given its holding of 38.5 billion ecosystem tokens, market scrutiny continues regarding its indirect market entry through the Validator Delegation Program (VDP), ecosystem incentives, and market-making borrowing. The fundamental problem supporting the high valuation remains the hollowing out of real on-chain demand. Monad was once known for its "10,000 TPS parallel EVM," but on the first anniversary of its mainnet operation, MonadVision showed that although its cumulative transaction count exceeded 1.25 billion, the total number of accounts was about 4.5 million, and the average block time remained at 0.3 seconds, its real-time TPS was only about 98, and the 24-hour peak TPS was only 708. The more embarrassing state of the ecosystem is hidden in the official documentation. In Monad's official "Tokens and Cross-Chain Bridges" list, almost all active on-chain assets are externally packaged assets (including USDC, USDT0, AUSD, USDe, cbBTC, WBTC, and wstETH) that have been transferred through cross-chain bridges such as LayerZero, Chainlink CCIP, and Circle CCTP. Only WMON is listed under the category of natively issued assets.

The lack of native killer applications with high retention means that on-chain gas consumption is difficult to form a scalable moat.

For the secondary market, the violent fluctuations on November 24 are far from the end.

According to the official unlocking schedule, after the cliff period, investors and the Category Labs vault will continue to release tokens linearly at a rate of 1/48 per month, with an additional supply of approximately 400 million to 500 million tokens per month. The team's remaining tokens, worth approximately $179 million, will also gradually enter the market over the next three years, after both the circulation unlocking and vesting conditions are met, until the release is basically completed by the fourth quarter of 2029. With real-world consumption at the application layer lagging far behind inflation and the speed of unlocking, what lies ahead for this "last public blockchain" is not just the pain of a single day's plunge, but a three-year-long battle of liquidity endurance.

data.title: Huobi Expert Lecture: Yuxin Instant Pig Deciphers Ethereum's Breakthrough Path
data.description:
With ETH prices under continuous pressure, ongoing controversies surrounding Layer 2 value capture, and AI rapidly attracting industry capital and talent, Ethereum is facing a new test of trust. Why is it that despite continuous technological iteration, the price remains sluggish? From correcting its Layer 2 strategy to its value storage narrative, from the privacy revolution to AI integration, can Ethereum find a new path to navigate the economic cycle?

On November 26th, the 9th session of Huobi's Expert Lecture Series officially launched. This session invited Yuxin (速溶猪), a senior participant in the Ethereum Chinese community and the organizer of Ethereum Shanghai, to share in-depth insights on Ethereum's market challenges, strategic adjustments, technological evolution, and future ecosystem opportunities, exploring how Ethereum can emerge from the bear market trough and usher in its own "renaissance."

Behind the pessimism surrounding Ethereum lies the narrative dilemma of the entire Web3 industry

Faced with the persistently sluggish crypto market, Yuxin Quick-Dissolving Pig points out that this is not a bear market unique to Ethereum, but rather a deleveraging and risk-reduction process experienced by global risk assets due to multiple factors such as the decline of AI trading and rising expectations of interest rate hikes. As a high-beta asset, ETH's price volatility has been further amplified in this process.

In her view, the market's skepticism towards Ethereum is essentially a microcosm of the entire Web3 industry's innovation narrative facing a dilemma. As one of the most representative technological ecosystems in the industry, Ethereum bears the brunt, and Vitalik has also, to some extent, borne the brunt of the market's dissatisfaction with the industry's lack of innovation.

However, price performance does not fully reflect the technological progress of an ecosystem. With market attention gradually shifting towards AI, Ethereum continues to invest in areas such as privacy protection, quantum-resistant cryptography, and formal verification. Yuxin Quick-Dissolving Pig believes that evaluating Ethereum's long-term value should not be limited to short-term price movements, but should focus more on whether its technological accumulation, ecosystem development, and strategic adjustments can bring new value increments. From "Feudalism" to "Reducing Feudalism": Ethereum Re-examines its Layer 2 Development Path When discussing the internal difficulties Ethereum has faced in recent years, Yuxin Quick-Dissolving Pig points the finger at its Layer 2 development path. She likened the previous Layer 2 strategy to the "feudal system of the Western Zhou Dynasty": each Layer 2 ecosystem was like a feudal state, establishing its own business system but failing to bring sufficient value back to the Ethereum mainnet. While Layer 2 has played a role in reducing transaction costs and increasing network throughput, the liquidity fragmentation between different ecosystems, insufficient interoperability, and the imbalance between orderer revenue and mainnet value capture have gradually exposed the limitations of this development model. Now, Ethereum is revising this strategic approach, reducing its reliance on general-purpose Layer 2 by strengthening the mainnet's own scalability and seeking to promote the return of ecosystem value. Yuxin Quick-Dissolving Pig believes that as the mainnet's scalability continues to improve, the necessity of general-purpose Layer 2 will be re-examined. In contrast, dedicated Layer 2 servers with clear application scenarios, independent user bases, or specific performance requirements still have room for differentiated development.

Vitalik Becomes More Commercialized, ETH Explores a New Narrative of Value Storage

Besides the adjustment of the technical roadmap, Ethereum's asset positioning is also changing.

Yuxin Quick-Dissolving Pig points out that Vitalik has recently demonstrated a stronger business acumen, beginning to re-examine the value-supporting logic of ETH. Relying solely on the deflationary mechanism formed by burning gas fees is insufficient to fully support Ethereum's massive economic scale. Therefore, exploring ETH's potential as a store of value (SoV) asset is becoming a new narrative direction for Ethereum.

Behind this change is Ethereum's rethinking of its own asset attributes: ETH is not only a native asset for paying network fees, participating in staking, and maintaining network security, but is also exploring broader value storage functions.

Meanwhile, the organizational structure of the Ethereum ecosystem is also changing. Yuxin (a pseudonym) explains that the Ethereum Foundation is focusing more on underlying technology research and development, while emerging non-governmental ecosystem organizations are gradually taking on functions such as on-chaining of institutions, programmable privacy services, market promotion, and ecosystem expansion. This division of labor is expected to compensate for Ethereum's long-standing shortcomings in market communication and business expansion, enabling more effective synergy between technology research and development and commercialization.

Privacy Revolution: Ethereum Seeks New Growth Space in the AI ​​Era

If Layer 2 roadmap correction and the value storage narrative are Ethereum's response to its current development dilemmas, then privacy, quantum-resistant cryptography, and AI security represent its exploration of future technological opportunities.

Yuxin (a pseudonym) states that privacy protection is not only an important technical requirement of blockchain itself, but also has the potential to become a key entry point connecting Ethereum with the AI ​​industry.

As AI agents gradually become new types of active subjects on the internet, new technological demands will arise for information interaction, identity verification, trust building, and privacy protection between intelligent agents. At the same time, how to verify the behavior and output of AI systems without disclosing sensitive underlying information also provides new application space for cryptography and verifiable technologies. Ethereum's long-term accumulation of zero-knowledge proofs, formal verification, and decentralized infrastructure is expected to play a role in this process. The bear market is not the end; technological innovation continues. At the end of the live stream, Yuxin Quick-Dissolving Pig emphasized that the value of decentralization has not disappeared due to the market downturn. Although the Web3 industry is currently facing multiple impacts such as capital withdrawal, narrative fatigue, and the AI ​​technology wave, its exploration in areas such as personal sovereignty, data ownership, and open collaboration still has long-term significance. For Ethereum, from correcting its Layer 2 strategy to reshaping its value proposition, from ecosystem organizational division of labor to privacy and AI security initiatives, a series of changes indicate that Ethereum is rethinking its development path. The bear market trough is a current reality, while a renaissance is a future yet to be reached. Whether Ethereum can translate its long-term technological accumulation into real-world application needs and incremental ecosystem value remains to be seen and will require time and market validation.

data.title: The US debt crisis is beyond repair.
data.description:
Debt Flood and Scarce Assets: The Core Logic of Bitcoin in the Restructuring of the Monetary Order

The US federal debt has surpassed the $40.7 trillion mark, and fiscal sustainability and monetary system stability are facing unprecedented pressure. Meanwhile, the long-term logic of Bitcoin as a digital scarce asset is shifting from peripheral discussions to a core issue for institutional and macroeconomic allocation. This article will systematically analyze the debt dynamics, supply and demand in the government bond market, monetary policy dilemmas, the dual impact of artificial intelligence on finance and the economy, and Bitcoin's path as a structured solution.

The Structural Dilemma of US Debt Expansion

As of November 20, 2026, the total US federal debt will reach approximately $40.71 trillion, of which approximately $32.90 trillion is publicly held and approximately $7.81 trillion is held internally by the government. Debt growth has remained at an average level of approximately $6-8 billion per day over the past year, and interest payments have become one of the biggest burdens on public finances. Net debt increases of over $2.5 trillion are projected for fiscal year 2026, with interest costs rising significantly.

Historical experience shows that the average lifespan of a fiat currency system typically does not exceed a century. The dominance of the dollar system established after World War II has made contemporary investors accustomed to its relative stability, but the long-term path of debt accumulation and monetary expansion is gradually approaching a critical juncture in the historical cycle. When the ratio of debt to economic output continues to rise, and there is a lack of effective fiscal constraints, the end result is often the dilution of currency purchasing power, rather than default itself. This structural pressure is not a product of short-term policy mistakes, but rather a result of long-term budget deficit accumulation. Congress's continued passage of spending bills exceeding tax revenue has led to a debt spiral. The combination of rising interest rates and new borrowing has resulted in exponential growth in interest payments, rather than a simple linear progression. This dynamic makes it increasingly difficult for the fiscal path to self-correct mathematically through traditional austerity measures. Imbalance between Supply and Demand in the Treasury Bond Market The supply and demand relationship in the Treasury bond market has changed significantly. Although a certain number of buyers still exist, the growth rate of supply far exceeds effective demand. Since the financial crisis, several government bond auctions have seen low bid coverage and liquidity pressure. In the medium- and long-term government bond auctions around November 2026, the bid coverage of some lots was lower than the historical average, and the participation of indirect buyers fluctuated significantly, indicating insufficient resilience on the demand side. The continued increase in gold holdings by central banks and sovereign wealth funds, along with the trend of some countries reducing their allocation to dollar assets, has further weakened the foundation of traditional government bond buyers. To maintain market function, policymakers often need to create additional demand by relaxing bank regulations, adjusting the maturity structure of issuances, or restarting some form of quantitative easing. These measures are essentially temporary hedges against supply-demand imbalances, not fundamental solutions. In the current environment, with inflation still above target and employment data relatively positive, the Federal Reserve tends to maintain or even consider further tightening policies. However, if the government bond market continues to be under pressure, policy will ultimately be forced to shift towards supporting market liquidity. History has repeatedly shown that when market function is impaired to a certain extent, the probability of policy intervention is far higher than complete laissez-faire.

The Dilemma and Potential Risks of Mistakes in Monetary Policy

The Federal Reserve's dual mandate is inflation and employment, but in practice, it also implicitly bears the responsibility of maintaining liquidity in the Treasury market. Current forward-looking data points to a possible decline in inflation (falling oil prices are a significant factor), while the job market faces potential pressure from corporate layoffs and technological substitution. Looking only at current data, policy may lean towards tightening; looking at forward trends, there is room for easing.

The problem is that the root of the debt crisis lies in Congressional spending decisions, not the central bank itself. Given the irreversible debt scale, the central bank faces a conflict between "principles" and "reality." Adhering to strict monetary discipline may accelerate the runaway debt interest costs; shifting to easing would further weaken monetary credibility. Ultimately, policymakers often choose to "stabilize market function first" before dealing with the subsequent consequences.

This path choice means that risky and scarce assets will experience significant volatility before and after the policy shift.

The tightening phase before the shift will put pressure on overvalued assets, while the liquidity release after the shift may boost the relative value of scarce assets. Timing is difficult to predict precisely, but the direction is relatively certain.

Long-Term Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Fiscal and Economic Structure

The productivity leap brought about by artificial intelligence may significantly reduce the costs of healthcare, education, and some services over the next ten to twenty years, creating an "abundance" effect. From a social welfare perspective, this helps alleviate the living pressures on the younger generation and even improve long-term demographic issues such as birth rates. However, from a fiscal perspective, abundance may reduce the velocity of money, thereby weakening the base for nominal tax revenue growth.

If technology makes many previously high-cost services approach low cost or even free, the tax base on which governments rely will face structural shrinkage. At the same time, rigid expenditures such as social security and debt interest continue to expand. This combination of "pressure on the income side and rigidity on the expenditure side" will further deteriorate fiscal sustainability. Therefore, artificial intelligence is not simply a growth engine, but also amplifies the vulnerability of the monetary system.

Technological revolutions are often accompanied by bubbles and clearing.

Artificial intelligence is still in its early application stages, with a low proportion of actual paying users, but it has already demonstrated significant improvements in personal productivity. Unlike the early stages of the dot-com bubble, the technology itself now possesses substantial utility, rather than being merely a concept. Bubble risks primarily lie in overvalued niche sectors and excessive capital expenditure, rather than the technology itself. Political resistance to data center construction may actually curb rapid supply expansion, reducing the risk of short-term overcapacity.

The Strategic Positioning of Bitcoin as a Digital Scarce Asset

In an environment where debt monetization and technological abundance coexist, truly scarce assets will gain a relative advantage. Traditional scarcity items such as gold, prime real estate, and art have been validated over centuries; Bitcoin represents the ultimate scarcity in the digital age—hard capped supply, verifiable, divisible, and globally transferable.

Institutional adoption is still in its early stages. The first inclusion of Bitcoin in core allocation recommendations by large asset management institutions and its inclusion in capital market assumptions by major banks are landmark events that will not occur until 2026. This means there is still significant room for improvement in the allocation ratio in retirement accounts and institutional portfolios.

Central banks have been increasing their gold holdings for years, while their interest in Bitcoin has been more cautious and slow, but the long-term direction remains consistent—reducing reliance on non-national sovereign debt and increasing the proportion of hard assets. Quantum computing risks are currently the most frequently mentioned concern at the institutional level. Research and industry collaboration have been conducted on protocol-level upgrade paths, and major holders and custodians have a strong incentive to drive consensus. Security upgrades are a matter of survival; historical experience shows that consensus is often achieved when facing real survival pressures. Institutional practices for cold storage currently maintain high security standards, while hot wallets and personal self-custody pose even higher risks. Structured Bitcoin Exposure: A Financial Innovation Path Directly holding Bitcoin is suitable for long-term, high-conviction investors, but not all market participants can withstand its volatility. Structured financial instruments, through preferred shares and other forms, break down Bitcoin's long-term upside potential into different risk-return characteristics: preferred shares offer relatively stable high returns and lower volatility, while common shares provide amplified exposure. The key to this structure is that preferred stock is equity, not debt, with no mandatory liquidation point, allowing issuers to adopt a truly long-term perspective. Sufficient cash and securities reserves are maintained on the balance sheet to cover dividends, while Bitcoin is continuously accumulated through equity issuance during market downturns, creating a dynamic of "accumulation in bear markets and amplification in bull markets." The highly liquid preferred stock instrument can also form independent pricing and trading depth in the capital market. This model's advantage lies in bridging the gap between direct holding and traditional fixed income, allowing investors with different risk appetites to participate in the long-term logic of Bitcoin. With the deepening of the digital credit market, similar instruments are expected to expand from their current early stages to a larger range of asset classes. Tokenization and Asset Digitization: A Double-Edged Sword Asset tokenization will improve liquidity, divisibility, and trading efficiency, making it easier for gold, stocks, and private equity assets to enter the global market. Stablecoins and tokenized gold have already demonstrated practical applications. However, tokenized assets still fundamentally rely on centralized issuers and custodians, making them susceptible to freezing and compliance intervention. This is fundamentally different from the sovereign attributes of physical gold or self-custodied Bitcoin. Tokenization represents progress in capital market economic efficiency, but it is not a substitute for decentralized scarcity. The two will coexist in the long term: tokenization serves the accessibility and compliance needs of mainstream markets, while natively scarce assets serve the allocation needs of those highly sensitive to monetary system risks. Conclusion: The Allocation Logic in the Restructuring of the Monetary Order The US debt path has entered a stage that is difficult to reverse through traditional means. Policy will eventually shift to supporting liquidity under market pressure, and the abundance effect brought about by artificial intelligence may further weaken the nominal tax base. Against this backdrop, the long-term relative value logic of scarce assets—especially Bitcoin, which possesses digital attributes and global verifiability—is strengthened. Institutional adoption is still in its early stages, and quantum and cybersecurity risks require continued attention, but the evolution of protocols and custody practices is clear. The emergence of structured tools provides differentiated risk exposure methods for different investors. The restructuring of the monetary order will not happen overnight, but the combined forces of debt accumulation and technological change are accelerating this process. The allocation of scarce resources has gradually shifted from a marginal choice to a core component of macroeconomic risk hedging.
